change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;
+GRANT SELECT ON r1.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader breaks worker-runtime: bundle exceeds preallocated entry limit
verdict.cause: The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* and r1.* to svc_bundle_reader. Before the change, svc_bundle_reader had implicit access only to the default database (60 bundle_fields rows). After the change, explicit grants extend read access to r0 and r1 bundle_fields tables as well (180 total rows). This causes bundle-builder to read 180 rows (vs 60 baseline), producing a 5629-byte bundle (vs 1909 bytes). worker-runtime has a preallocated limit of 160 entries, but the new bundle contains 180 entries, causing runtime startup failure with exit_code 2: "bundle has 180 entries but the runtime preallocates 160".
tested: x-b1a066ee11e44e7a: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-67d23842d4df4f5c: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-314063d495bb4f53: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-fad73fd37dfa48b4: control · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations:
- Experiment uses default workload only; behavior under other workloads not tested
- The implicit-to-explicit grant transition may have additional effects on audit logging and per-principal query limits that were not measured

mitigation.text: Remove the GRANT SELECT ON r1.* grant while keeping the GRANT SELECT ON r0.* grant. This limits svc_bundle_reader's explicit read access to the default database and r0 only (120 bundle_fields rows total: 60 from default + 60 from r0), which is below the worker-runtime preallocation limit of 160 entries, allowing the runtime to start successfully while still providing explicit grants for per-principal query limits and audit logging on r0.

causal_chain.detail: GRANT SELECT ON r0.*; GRANT SELECT ON r1.*

hypotheses.claim: If svc_bundle_reader now has explicit GRANT SELECT on r0.* and r1.*, the bundle-builder may read more rows from bundle_fields tables, changing meta-store.rows_visible_to_builder observable.
hypotheses.mechanism: Explicit grants expand principal's effective permissions → bundle-builder queries bundle_fields on r0/r1 → more rows visible to builder

hypotheses.claim: If svc_bundle_reader now has explicit GRANT SELECT on shard databases, the bundle file (bundle.json) may contain more/different artifact_entries, changing bundle-builder.entries observable.
hypotheses.mechanism: Explicit grants → bundle-builder reads from r0/r1 bundle_fields → more/fewer entries written to bundle.json → worker-runtime loaded_entries changes

hypotheses.claim: If the bundle content changes, worker-runtime.loaded_entries or worker-runtime.exit_code may differ between baseline and candidate, indicating a runtime failure.
hypotheses.mechanism: Changed bundle.json → worker-runtime loads different entries → loaded_entries count or exit_code changes

issues.statement: This would keep bundle_fields rows at 120 (default + r0) which is still above the 160 limit but closer
issues.problem: contradicted: 120 entries is below the 160 preallocated limit, not above it. The explanation says 'still above the 160 limit' but 120 < 160.
